turns.q:
Your response was: "Looked at it. Most of it made sense. One thing didn't — two buttons at the bottom. Went to the wrong one first. Darker one drew my eye. That wasn't the action I needed."

We want to understand what you meant by "went to the wrong one first", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The visual weight and prominence of the "Continue Shopping" button compared to the "Place Order" button.
B) The placement of the "Continue Shopping" button above the "Place Order" button in the layout.
C) The lack of clear distinction between the two primary actions at the bottom of the screen.
D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
What specific visual characteristics of the "Continue Shopping" button make it stand out more than the "Place Order" button in this layout?
turns.a: 'Continue Shopping.' Heavier. More presence. 'Place Order' is the lighter one.

turns.q: If a developer built this layout exactly as shown, how would that visual weight affect someone's ability to identify the primary action they need to take?
turns.a: Eye went to the wrong one. The heavier button looked like the step to take. It wasn't.

turns.q: Does that visual weight make the primary action harder to locate, or just more confusing once it is found?
turns.a: Said this. Eye goes to the wrong button. Re-read required.

turns.q: When the eye goes to the wrong button first, what does that tell you about how the layout's structure communicates the priority of these two actions?
turns.a: 'Continue Shopping' pulled the eye every scan. 'Place Order' didn't. Almost went the wrong direction. Re-read both before I moved.

turns.q: What would need to be reorganized in this layout for that visual weight issue not to be an issue?
turns.a: 'Place Order' needs a solid fill. 'Continue Shopping' needs ghost treatment — outline only or text link. Right now the visual treatment is inverted. Solid fill goes on the primary CTA. Always.
